title: Everton expected to finalise CMC Markets deal to replace Stake as primary shirt sponsor
content:
Everton are expected to finalise a deal with CMC Markets which will see the financial services firm replace Stake on the front of their shirt from next season.

The Merseyside club have been looking for a new sponsor to replace Stake, the Australian bookmaker and online cryptocurrency casino, with new government legislation prohibiting logos of gambling firms from appearing on the front of Premier League shirts from next season.

After months of talks, CMC has emerged as the clear frontrunner to take over when Stake’s deal expires at the end of June, according to sources briefed on matters, speaking confidentially as they were not authorised to do so publicly. Should the move be confirmed, reports elsewhere have suggested that the company set up by Conservative peer Lord Cruddas will pay a figure in the region of £30million ($40.3m) across a three-year period.

That would be a comparable sum to the near £10m per-year deal Everton agreed with Stake in 2022, which was billed as a club record at the time, and would likely be seen as a success at Everton given the amount of clubs searching for new front-of-shirt sponsors for next season.

That market is proven to be challenging for many Premier League clubs, some of whom may end up signing reduced deals or head into the new season with no partner at all, but sleeve sponsorships are likely to be one growth area this summer.

With legislation only prohibiting gambling partners from appearing on the front of shirts, some firms, like Stake, are expected to migrate onto sleeves instead. A new sleeve sponsorship deal has not been confirmed by Everton or the Australian bookmaker, but is also expected to be concluded in time for the new season.

Headquartered in London, CMC is a global investment and trading platform that posted a net operating income of £340m in 2025, per a release last June. It has been looking to expand its sponsorship portfolio and has also been linked to a potential deal with Premier League side Fulham.

One of CMC’s services is spread betting, described on its own website as “a popular form of derivative trading that enables you to speculate on the price movements of financial assets, such as indices, forex, commodities, and shares, without owning the underlying asset”.

There is confidence from those with knowledge of CMC’s operations that it will be permissible as a new front-of-shirt sponsor under new Premier League regulations. One possible explanation is that CMC engages in other activities apart from spread betting, but neither the Premier League nor Everton has yet publicly commented on the matter.

CMC has also sponsored the Aussie Rules side St Kilda since 2022.

Stake, meanwhile, left the UK market in February 2025 after the country’s Gambling Commission (GC) launched an investigation into a company-branded advert featuring a pornographic actress. Stake still operates internationally and has sponsored the Kick Sauber F1 team.

Everton, CMC Markets, Stake and the Premier League were all approached for comment.
